title: spec review: S2a2 packet memory wiring: HOT view plus filtered WARM search feed the gotchas and decisions packet sections in shadow, decision_log kind memory_retrieval, promotion feature memory_tiers (P1, P3, P5 groundwork)
spec:
In orchestrator/spawn.py _packet_body: today the gotchas section comes from memory_recall over notes+bus (up to 5 hits) and the decisions section from grep of decisions.md in the worktree. Add a second source: hot = memory_hot.build (read HOT.md when fresh, i.e. store unchanged since the last build, else rebuild) and warm = memory_store.search(query from task title + scope basenames, kind in (gotcha, decision, architecture), file filter per scope path, limit 8) merged and deduplicated by id, rendered with the same one-line format, capped by [memory].packet_hot_tokens (default 1200, dated comment). Mode [memory].mode (off|shadow|active; add as shadow with a dated comment) and promotion FEATURES entry memory_tiers (orchestrator/promotion.py) with criteria: at least 30 decision_log rows of kind memory_retrieval in 7 days and a measured presented-token reduction with no rise in fix rounds (state the criteria in the feature entry as the other features do). Shadow: present the legacy sections unchanged, compute the tiered sections and record one decision_log row kind memory_retrieval (add it to decision_log.KINDS) with candidates (record ids with tier and score), selected (ids the tiered path would present), legacy_ids (the hits the legacy path presented), tokens_legacy, tokens_tiered, mode, subject task id. Active: present the tiered sections and still record the row. Off: legacy only. packet_meta gains memory_mode and memory_ids. The row must never raise into packet building (guard, log a warning). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/07-hot-memory.md gains a section on packet wiring and the shadow comparison measured on three real tasks of this repository (ids, tokens_legacy vs tokens_tiered).
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_memory_shadow_keeps_legacy_sections_and_logs_row (shadow: legacy text presented, memory_retrieval row with both token counts)
tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_memory_active_presents_tiered_sections (active: HOT and warm hits presented, capped by packet_hot_tokens)

risks.issue: Spec says memory_tiers should 'state the criteria in the feature entry as the other features do,' but no existing FEATURES entry carries per-feature criteria — every entry is only {table,key,modes,default,evidence} (see jev_routing, planner_routing, context_router, etc.) and promotion.evaluate() applies one global CRITERIA dict (min_samples=20, first_pass_delta, fix_rounds_delta, gate_success_delta, review_findings_delta, security_ok) to all features uniformly via _criteria(cfg). The spec's '30 decision_log rows of kind memory_retrieval in 7 days' is a time-windowed count that collect()/evaluate() has no mechanism for (collect() only ever returns a flat n). As written this asks for architecture that doesn't exist and contradicts the stated 'as other features do' precedent, so test_memory_tiers_feature_registered_with_criteria is unverifiable against the real FEATURES shape.

CONTEXT_KINDS already declares a kind literally named 'retrieval' (line 21) that is unused anywhere in the repo (grep finds only its declaration). The spec adds a new, separate 'memory_retrieval' kind without addressing this pre-existing near-duplicate, which a reviewer will flag as redundant/confusing naming.

_packet_body's overall body is capped at 4800 chars by a trim loop (lines 683-697) driven by a fixed `trimmable` tuple of section names, mirroring how _shadow_route's routed sections already interact with it via _trim_routed_item. The spec's new hot/warm sections and their separate packet_hot_tokens (1200 token) cap aren't reconciled with this existing loop — unclear if 'hot'/'warm' join `trimmable`, are exempt, or whether the two caps double-constrain the same content.

search() only accepts a single scalar `kind=` value (equality match, not an IN-list) per its signature at line 279. The spec's 'kind in (gotcha, decision, architecture)' phrasing implies one query with multiple kinds; the executor actually needs three separate search() calls merged/deduplicated by id, which the spec should state explicitly to avoid a wrong-API assumption.

Every other shadow-mode toggle in this file pairs its dated comment with an explicit revert instruction (e.g. context_router: 'revert by setting mode back to "off"', tool_disclosure: same pattern) — that comment is this repo's actual rollback mechanism for config-gated features. The spec only says 'add as shadow with a dated comment' and doesn't require the revert instruction text.

Spec says packet building should 'read HOT.md when fresh, i.e. store unchanged since the last build, else rebuild' but memory_hot.build() has no freshness check — it always recomputes and rewrites HOT.md. Since memory_hot.py is out of scope, the freshness signal must live in spawn.py, but the spec doesn't say what to compare (e.g. index.sqlite mtime vs HOT.md mtime, the same mtime-signature pattern already used in orchestrator/bus.py:258); left unspecified, this diverges between an implementer's reading and a reviewer's expectation.

suggested_spec_changes: Drop the 'state criteria in the feature entry as other features do' framing for memory_tiers; either register it with the same {table,key,modes,default,evidence} shape as every other FEATURES entry and let it use the global CRITERIA thresholds via evaluate()/collect(), or explicitly say this is new per-feature-criteria infrastructure (and that evaluate()/_criteria() needs new code to support it) rather than implying precedent that doesn't exist.
Clarify whether the new memory_retrieval decision_log kind should reuse the existing unused 'retrieval' kind in CONTEXT_KINDS instead of adding a near-duplicate.

Specify how the new hot/warm packet sections interact with _packet_body's existing 4800-char trim loop and `trimmable` tuple, and whether packet_hot_tokens is a sub-budget inside that cap or independent.
State that memory_store.search must be called once per kind (gotcha, decision, architecture) and merged/deduplicated by id, since search() takes a single scalar kind, not a list.
Specify the exact freshness check for reusing HOT.md (e.g. compare .orchestrator/memory/index.sqlite mtime against HOT.md mtime) so implementation doesn't invent an ad hoc signal.

Note that decision_log.record() requires hard_constraints, deterministic, and selected as well as the listed fields (candidates, legacy_ids, tokens_legacy, tokens_tiered, mode, subject); state what to pass for hard_constraints/deterministic when not applicable, consistent with other shadow call sites.
